title: Test each candidate against the best reply
outcomes: Tests each candidate against the opponent's best reply instead of the reply that suits the plan
Finds a surviving move on a self-made list in positions where the first idea fails
Keeps a quiet move on the list when forcing candidates fail
Recognises a position where the first idea is right, or the move is forced, and stops listing

steps.text: You have met the candidate list in **Candidates and short lines**. This lesson adds one test: does a candidate **survive the opponent's best reply**? Judge it against his strongest answer, not the one you hope for. Often the first idea fails this test and a different move on the list passes. Your job is to find that move before you play.

steps.caption: The first idea is a forcing move. Does it survive the reply?

line.say: Candidate one: Qxg4+, a capture. It is forcing, so it comes first on the list.
A reply to test: Kc2. Against it Qxg4+ ends far below Qxf1+, the engine's first choice.

claims.statement: Qxg4+ is at least 300 centipawns worse than the best move (depth 16).
Qxf1+ is the engine's first choice (depth 16).
With best play the side to move stands at least two pawns better (depth 16).

steps.text: **When this pays.** Testing every candidate against its best reply costs time. It pays when the position is not forced and more than one plan is plausible. **Rule of thumb:** test the forcing candidate first; if it fails, move down the list. Keep a quiet move on the list: sometimes it is the only one that survives. It is wasted when the first idea is plainly right or only one move is legal.

steps.title: The list pays, the quiet survivor, nothing to list
steps.prompt: Predict first: in which position does a forcing move fail and another forcing move survive, in which is a quiet move the only survivor, and in which is there nothing to list? Then check.

steps.text: **What the app does for you now, and when it stops.** The candidate-list box from **Candidates and short lines** stays beside the board in mixed practice, hidden until you open it; the app notes when you do. The next three items are silent: no hints and no engine. One of them may need no list at all.
